summary: Outlier detection for interval-valued data has lacked an explanation layer. The paper derives closed-form Shapley values and a Shapley interaction index for the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance under the IMCD estimator, decomposing outlyingness into centers, ranges, and cross-terms. On the Cars and Spotify datasets it illustrates variable-level explanations and flags outliers consistent with domain knowledge.

why: The AIDA repository is a complete, self-contained R package: it ships the intCars.rda data, the IMCD estimator (R/IMCD.r), farness transform (R/farness.r), outlier flagging (R/int_outliers.r), and two vignettes (IMCD_examples.Rmd, Shapley_examples.Rmd) plus executed scripts in inst/doc/ that perform exactly the Cars analysis behind C1-C6 (reweighted IMCD with ~75% subset, 0.9 farness cutoff, Shapley barplot of the six largest distances). No weights, no downloads and no dead frameworks: the only needs are an R runtime and CRAN dependencies.
est_runtime: ~20-30 min: ~10-15 min to install R (if absent) and compile/install AIDA + CRAN deps, ~1-2 min to run the Cars IMCD + farness + Shapley vignette chunk
blockers: This is an R package, not Python: requires installing R plus CRAN dependencies (MAINT.Data, rrcov/robustbase, ggplot2, etc.), which is the bulk of the setup time
MAINT.Data is pinned at version 2.8.0 in the paper; newer CRAN versions may change the Cars import path slightly
IMCD subset selection is stochastic: reaching exactly the five named flags may require fixing the seed / repeating the random subset draw
Nothing renders offline: vignette figures need ggplot2 and the package built/installed (R CMD INSTALL) before the .Rmd will knit

approach: The AIDA repository is an R package, but the sandbox can only execute Python/pip/git, so the plan uses the shipped AIDA sources and vignettes as the executable specification and ports only the tiny Cars pipeline to Python. We read data/intCars.rda with pyreadr/rdata, extract the interval bounds and car labels, then port the reweighted IMCD, farness transform, squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance, and closed-form Shapley/interaction formulas line-by-line from R/IMCD.r, R/farness.r, R/int_distances.r, and R/Shapley.r. The primary target is C1: reproduce the five Figure 1 outlier labels with h=20, farness cutoff 0.9, and strict score>0.9 flagging. The same fit is reused for the Figure 2a top-six and Figure 3 Shapley diagnostics. C2-C6 are recorded in results/metrics.json as intermediate checks rather than separate experiments.
steps: Use Python to ensure third_party/AIDA exists; if not, run git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catarinaploureiro/AIDA.git third_party/AIDA. Do not modify author files.
Install Python dependencies needed for parsing RData: pip install pyreadr rdata; keep preinstalled numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib.

Inspect third_party/AIDA/data/intCars.rda from Python. First try pyreadr; if the intData S4 object is not directly convertible, use rdata to recursively dump object classes and attributes and locate slots LowerBounds, UpperBounds, Centers, Ranges, and Class/labels. Use man/ and R/intData_class.r to identify slot names.

Build the Cars matrix as n=27, p=4 lower/upper arrays with car-model labels. Confirm the four variables are lnPrice, Engine Capacity, Top Speed, and Acceleration; if Price is not already logged, apply natural log to both Price bounds and rename to lnPrice. Drop only the class variable from distance computations.
Compute interval centers c=(a+b)/2 and ranges r=b-a for the four variables. Assert finite values, positive ranges, and no accidental extra variables.
Port the symbolic covariance construction from R/int_cov.r using the Uniform[-1,1] latent moments; verify the 4x4 covariance matrix is symmetric positive definite on the full data.

Implement IMCD in src/imcd.py: for each random start draw h=20 observations, compute symbolic covariance determinant, perform concentration C-steps retaining the h smallest robust distances, and keep the subset with the smallest determinant. Use five seed blocks of 2000 starts and select the best determinant; verify determinant stability across blocks.

Reweight the best IMCD fit: compute farness scores for all 27 observations using the current center/covariance, retain observations with score <= 0.9, recompute the robust barycenter and covariance, and iterate until the retained set is stable. Record the initial h subset size and final reweighted inlier count.

Port the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance from R/int_distances.r and compute distances and farness scores for all 27 Cars observations. Assert all distances and scores are finite and farness scores lie in [0,1].

Flag observations with farness score strictly greater than 0.9. Record the flagged labels in descending squared-distance order. Compare the count to 5 and the labels to MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, and HondaNSK.

Compute Shapley values for all observations using the closed-form expression ported from R/Shapley.r. For Cars set Psi=0 and cross center-range terms to zero per the symmetric uniform assumption. Check that sum_j phi_j equals the squared distance to numerical tolerance 1e-8.
Select the six observations with the largest squared distances, as in Figure 2a, regardless of outlier flag. Confirm the set contains the five expected outliers and Bmwserie7.
Compute the Shapley interaction matrix from Equations (10)-(12), setting diagonal terms so each row sums to that observation's Shapley value. Produce the Ferrari interaction tile data for Figure 3b.

Generate results/figures/cars_farness_outliers.png, cars_shapley_top6.png, cars_center_range_decomp.png, and ferrari_interaction_tile.png. Plot expected versus computed labels where useful for debugging.

Write results/metrics.json with a claim-level section for C1-C6 plus diagnostic arrays: car labels, distances, farness scores, flagged labels, top-six labels/order, h and h-percent, final reweighted count, Shapley efficiency errors, and maximum absolute cross center-range term.
Run python reproduce.py for the full result and verify metrics.json contains C1 count/labels and all intermediate checks. Keep the full run deterministic with the configured seed.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: load intCars and assert shape 27x4, compute centers/ranges, fit IMCD with h=20 and 50 random starts for one seed block, compute distances and farness scores, and run Shapley values for the first observation. Assert finite outputs, covariance determinant >0, and Shapley efficiency error <1e-8. Write results/smoke.json and exit without making full figures. Target runtime <90 seconds.
intermediate_checks: Dataset check: intCars has exactly 27 rows, 4 interval variables, and labels including the five expected car names; class labels are present but excluded from distances.
Preprocessing check: lnPrice lower/upper bounds are on log scale; EngCap, Top Speed, Acceleration are untouched; no extra standardization is applied.
Geometry check: all ranges positive; centers/ranges finite; symbolic covariance symmetric positive definite; condition number below 1e12.
Subset check: h=20, h/n=74.07%, reported as approximately 75%; final reweighted inlier count at score<=0.9 is recorded separately.
IMCD stability check: best covariance determinant agrees across five independent seed blocks to relative tolerance 1e-6; if not, increase starts before proceeding.
Distance sanity check: a classical non-robust interval Mahalanobis baseline should rank the same suspected outliers near the top; large disagreement signals an IMCD/porting bug.
Farness check: all scores in [0,1], values around the 0.9 cutoff are printed with labels so a borderline flag is visible.
C1 check: flagged count must be 5 for exact label match, and within 2 observations for the tolerance-based claim.
C3/C10 check: top six by descending squared distance must include the five expected outliers plus Bmwserie7, with Bmwserie7 present even if not flagged.
Shapley efficiency check: for every observation, |sum(phi)-distance| <= 1e-8.
C6 check: maximum absolute cross centers-ranges Shapley contribution is <= 1e-10 for all Cars observations.
Interaction check: for Ferrari, row sums of the interaction matrix equal the Shapley values to tolerance 1e-8.
budget_plan: Total ~25 minutes. Setup 6-8 min: git clone and pip install pyreadr/rdata plus data introspection. Smoke 1-2 min: 50-start IMCD and one-observation Shapley check. Full fit 6-8 min: five seed blocks of 2000 starts on 27x20 subsets, reweighting, Shapley values and interactions. Figures/metrics 2-3 min. Reserve 4-5 min for debugging S4 extraction or a borderline farness flag; if IMCD starts are slow, reduce to 1000 starts per block only after confirming determinant stability.

    1| #' Farness Estimation
    2| #' 
    3| #' Estimate farness from a distance vector in order to identify outlier observations.
    4| #' 
    5| #' @param dist Vector of distances of each observation.
    6| #' @param cutoff_value Optional cutoff value between 0 and 1 to flag outliers. If provided, the function returns both the farness probabilities and the cutoff distance value in the original distance scale.
    7| #' @return  Either a vector of farness probabilities for each observation (if \code{cutoff_value} is not provided) or a list containing (if \code{cutoff_value} is provided):
    8| #' \item{\code{farness_probs}}{A vector of farness probabilities for each observation. Values between 0 and 1.}
    9| #' \item{\code{cutoff_value}}{The cutoff distance value in the original distance scale corresponding to the specified \code{cutoff_value} probability.}
   10| #' @references J. Raymaekers and P.J. Rousseeuw (2021). Transforming variables to central normality. Machine Learning. \doi{10.1007/s10994-021-05960-5}
   11| #' @references Based on the \code{cellWise} package: Raymaekers J, Rousseeuw P (2023). _cellWise: Analyzing Data with Cellwise Outliers_. R package version 2.5.3, \url{https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=cellWise}.
   12| #' @export
   13| #' @examples
   14| #' data(creditcard)
   15| #' credit_card_int <- creditcard$intData
   16| #' 
   17| #' # Compute squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance
   18| #' credit_card_dist <- IMah_dist(credit_card_int)
   19| #' 
   20| #' credit_card_farness <- farness(credit_card_dist, cutoff_value = 0.9)
   21| farness <- function(dist, cutoff_value=NULL) {
   22|     indnz <- which(dist > 1e-10)
   23|     farnz <- dist[indnz]
   24| 
   25|     # scale the distances
   26|     farloc <- median(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
   27|     farsca <- mad(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
   28|     if (farsca < 1e-10) {farsca <- sd(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)}
   29|     sfar <- scale(farnz, center = farloc, scale = farsca)
   30| 
   31|     # apply Yeo-Johnson transformation
   32|     YJout  <- cellWise::transfo(X = sfar, type = "YJ", robust = TRUE, standardize = FALSE, checkPars = list(silent = TRUE))
   33|     xt <- YJout$Y
   34| 
   35|     # scale the transformed distances
   36|     tfarloc <- median(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
   37|     tfarsca <- mad(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
   38|     zt <- scale(xt, tfarloc, tfarsca)
   39|     
   40|     # obtain final probabilities
   41|     probs <- rep(0, length(dist))
   42|     probs[indnz] <- pnorm(zt)
   43|     
   44|     names(probs) <- names(dist)
   45| 
   46|     # cutoff value
   47|     if (!is.null(cutoff_value)) {
   48|         if (cutoff_value>1||cutoff_value<0) stop("cutoff_value must be between 0 and 1")
   49|         cutoff_value <- qnorm(cutoff_value)
   50|         cutoff_value <- cutoff_value * tfarsca + tfarloc
   51|         cutoff_value <- cellWise::transfo_transformback(Ynew = cutoff_value, transfo.out = YJout)
   52|         cutof

  250| #' @references Loureiro, C. P., Oliveira, M. R., Brito, P., & Oliveira, L. (2026). 
  251| #' Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data.
  252| #' arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.26307. \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26307}
  253| #' 
  254| #' @examples
  255| #' # Create intData object
  256| #' data(creditcard)
  257| #' credit_card_int <- creditcard$intData
  258| #' 
  259| #' # Compute Shapley interaction indices based on the mean and covariance matrix estimated by IMCD
  260| #' credit_card_shap_inter <- int_Shapley_interaction(credit_card_int)
  261| #' @export
  262| int_Shapley_interaction <- function(data,mean_c=NULL,mean_r=NULL,cov=NULL){
  263| 
  264|     if(!inherits(data,"intData")) stop("Argument data is not an object of class intData\n")
  265| 
  266|     C <- as.matrix(data@Centers)
  267|     R <- as.matrix(data@Ranges)
  268|     param <- data@LatentParam
  269|     case <- data@LatentCase
  270| 
  271|     if(is.null(mean_c) || is.null(mean_r) || is.null(cov)){
  272|         IMCD_res <- IMCD(data,m=floor(data@NObs*0.75))
  273|         if(is.null(cov)) cov <- IMCD_res$cov_IMCD
  274|         if(is.null(mean_c)) mean_c <- IMCD_res$mean_IMCD_c
  275|         if(is.null(mean_r)) mean_r <- IMCD_res$mean_IMCD_r
  276|     }
  277| 
  278|     cov_inv <- safe_solve_cov(cov)
  279|     shapley_interaction <- list()
  280| 
  281|     for(i in 1:data@NObs){
  282|         c_0 <- C[i,]-mean_c
  283|         r_0 <- R[i,]-mean_r
  284|         if (case=="U_id_symmetric"){
  285|             delta <- param[[1]]
  286|             inter_shapley <- 2*tcrossprod(c_0)*cov_inv + 2*delta*tcrossprod(r_0)*cov_inv
  287|         }else if (case=="U_id"){
  288|             delta <- param[[1]]
  289|             U_mean <- param[[2]]
  290|             inter_shapley <- 2*tcrossprod(c_0)*cov_inv + 2*delta*tcrossprod(r_0)*cov_inv + 
  291|                     + U_mean*tcrossprod(c_0,r_0)*cov_inv + U_mean*tcrossprod(r_0,c_0)*cov_inv
  292|         }else if (case=="General"){
  293|             e_UU <- param[[1]]
  294|             psi <- param[[2]]
  295|             inter_shapley <- 2*tcrossprod(c_0)*cov_inv + 1/2*tcrossprod(r_0)*e_UU*cov_inv +
  296|                     + tcrossprod(c_0,r_0)*(cov_inv%*%psi) + tcrossprod(r_0,c_0)*(psi%*%cov_inv)
  297|         }
  298|         inter_shapley <- inter_shapley - diag(rowSums(inter_shapley/2))
  299|         rownames(inter_shapley) <- colnames(inter_shapley) <- colnames(data)
  300|         shapley_interaction[[rownames(data)[i]]] <- inter_shapley
  301|     }
  302|     return(shapley_interaction)

formations were subsequently applied, including logarithmic scaling for tempo and loudness,

and upper bounds of the intervals, respectively. The final dataset consists of 111 genres and
11 audio features, with each interval-valued observation representing a median of 800 tracks.

"""Interval algebra for the symbolic (Interval-Mahalanobis) pipeline.

Ports of the AIDA R helpers (repo/R/int_cov.r, repo/R/int_distances.r):

* ``int_mean_z`` : weighted mean of the interval centers.
* ``int_cov_z``  : symbolic covariance matrix for the ``U_id_symmetric`` latent
  case, i.e.  Sigma = S_cc/m - m_c m_c' + delta (S_rr/m - m_r m_r')  with
  delta = E(U^2)/4 = 1/12 for U ~ Uniform[-1,1].
* ``IMah_dist``  : squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance
      d2_i = (c_i-mu_c)' Sigma^-1 (c_i-mu_c) + delta (r_i-mu_r)' Sigma^-1 (r_i-mu_r)
* ``Mallows_dist``: squared Mallows distance (latent-variable formulation).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def interval_repr(lower: np.ndarray, upper: np.ndarray):
    """Centers c=(a+b)/2 and ranges r=b-a of interval bounds."""
    lower = np.asarray(lower, dtype=float)
    upper = np.asarray(upper, dtype=float)
    return (lower + upper) / 2.0, (upper - lower)


def symbolic_cov(z: np.ndarray, C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, delta: float):
    """int_cov_z(z, data) for the U_id_symmetric latent case.

    z : (n,) indicator/weight vector (entries >= 0, sum m = sum z)
    C : (n, p) centers, R : (n, p) ranges, delta = E(U^2)/4.
    """
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    m = z.sum()
    Cz = C.T @ z                       # sum_j z_j c_j  (p,)
    Rz = R.T @ z
    Scc = (C * z[:, None]).T @ C       # sum_j z_j c_j c_j'
    Srr = (R * z[:, None]).T @ R
    sigma = (Scc / m - np.outer(Cz / m, Cz / m)
             + delta * (Srr / m - np.outer(Rz / m, Rz / m)))
    return sigma


def symbolic_mean(z: np.ndarray, C: np.ndarray):
    """int_mean_z: z-weighted mean of the centers."""
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    return (C.T @ z) / z.sum()


def imahalanobis2(C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, mean_c: np.ndarray,
                  mean_r: np.ndarray, cov_inv: np.ndarray, delta: float):
    """Squared Interval-Mahalanobis distances of all rows to the barycenter.

    cov_inv is the *inverse* of the symbolic covariance matrix (R's
    mahalanobis(..., inverted=TRUE) convention in AIDA).
    """
    dc = C - mean_c[None, :]
    dr = R - mean_r[None, :]
    dc = dc - dc.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True) * 0  # no-op, keeps shape clarity
    q_c = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", dc, cov_inv, dc)
    q_r = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", dr, cov_inv, dr)
    return q_c + delta * q_r


def imahalanobis2_one(c: np.ndarray, r: np.ndarray, mean_c: np.ndarray,
                      mean_r: np.ndarray, cov_inv: np.ndarray, delta: float):
    """Squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance of a single observation."""
    dc = c - mean_c
    dr = r - mean_r
    return float(dc @ cov_inv @ dc + delta * (dr @ cov_inv @ dr))


def mallows_dist(C: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, mean_c: np.ndarray,
                 mean_r: np.ndarray, cov_inv: np.ndarray, delta: float):
    """Squared Mallows distances (deterministic-latent representation).

    AIDA's Mallows_dist uses the same algebra as IMah_dist for the
    U_id_symmetric case, so the robust and classical Mallows distances agree
    with the interval distances here; both are reported for the sanity check.
    """
    return imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov_inv, delta)


def classical_mahalanobis2(C: np.ndarray, cov: np.ndarray):
    """Non-robust classical Mahalanobis distances of the centers (sanity)."""
    mu = C.mean(axis=0)
    S = np.cov(C, rowvar=False)
    Si = np.linalg.inv(S)
    dc = C - mu[None, :]
    return np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", dc, Si, dc)

"""Reweighted IMCD estimator (port of AIDA repo/R/IMCD.r).

Algorithm (smallIMCD + reweighting), n = 27, p = 4, h = 20:

1. ``draw_z`` : draw p+1 = 5 random observations, build their symbolic
   covariance; while the covariance is singular add random observations.
2. ``pick10`` : two C-steps on every random start, keep the ten subsets with
   the smallest symbolic covariance determinant.
3. ``step_it``: iterate C-steps (assign the h observations with the smallest
   squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance, recompute the symbolic covariance)
   until the determinant stops decreasing.
4. Reweighting: farness outlier scores of the raw IMCD distances, keep the
   observations with score <= 0.9 and recompute the barycenter/covariance on
   that subset (cutoff="farness", cutoff_lvl=0.9 in AIDA's IMCD()).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from interval_ops import (imahalanobis2, imahalanobis2_one, symbolic_cov,
                          symbolic_mean)


def c_step(z, m, C, R, delta):
    """One C-step: reassign to the h closest observations, refit."""
    n = C.shape[0]
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    z_active = z > 0.5
    sigma = symbolic_cov(z_active.astype(float), C, R, delta)
    try:
        cov_inv = np.linalg.inv(sigma)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        cov_inv = np.linalg.pinv(sigma)
    mean_c = symbolic_mean(z_active.astype(float), C)
    mean_r = (R.T @ z_active) / z_active.sum()
    d2 = imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov_inv, delta)
    updated = np.zeros(n)
    updated[np.argsort(d2, kind="stable")[:m]] = 1.0
    sigma2 = symbolic_cov(updated, C, R, delta)
    det2 = float(np.linalg.det(sigma2))
    mean_c = symbolic_mean(updated, C)
    mean_r = (R.T @ updated) / m
    return dict(z=updated, S=sigma2, det=det2,
                mean_c=mean_c, mean_r=mean_r, d2=d2)


def draw_z(m, C, R, delta, rng):
    """Random h-subset (AIDA draw_z): p+1 seeds, grow until non-singular."""
    n, p = C.shape
    nseed = p + 1
    j = rng.permutation(n)[:nseed].copy()
    z = np.zeros(n)
    z[j] = 1.0
    det = -np.inf
    sigma = None
    while True:
        sigma = symbolic_cov(z, C, R, delta)
        det = float(np.linalg.det(sigma))
        if det != 0.0 or len(j) >= n - 1:
            break
        k = int(rng.integers(0, n))
        if z[k] == 0:
            j = np.append(j, k)
            z[k] = 1.0
    return z, sigma, det


def pick10(z_all, m, C, R, delta, two_steps=True):
    """Keep the 10 best subsets after two C-steps (AIDA pick10)."""
    scored = []
    for z in z_all:
        s = c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
        if two_steps:
            s = c_step(s["z"], m, C, R, delta)
        scored.append((s["det"], s))
    scored.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
    return [s for _, s in scored[:10]]


def step_it(z, m, C, R, delta, max_iter=100, tol=1e-10):
    """Iterate C-steps until the determinant stops decreasing."""
    s = c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
    det_old = s["det"]
    for _ in range(max_iter):
        s = c_step(s["z"], m, C, R, delta)
        det_new = s["det"]
        if det_old > det_new and det_new > 0.0:
            det_old = det_new
        else:
            break
        if abs(det_old - det_new) <= tol * max(abs(det_old), 1.0):
            break
    return s


def small_imcd(m, C, R, delta, nstarts=500, seed=0):
    """AIDA smallIMCD: nstarts random subsets -> 10 best -> full convergence."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    z_all = [draw_z(m, C, R, delta, rng)[0] for _ in range(nstarts)]
    best10 = pick10(z_all, m, C, R, delta)
    final = [step_it(s["z"], m, C, R, delta) for s in best10]
    best = min(final, key=lambda s: s["det"])
    return best


def imcd(m, C, R, delta, nstarts=500, seed=0):
    """Raw (unreweighted) IMCD fit, as in AIDA's IMCD() before reweighting."""
    return small_imcd(m, C, R, delta, nstarts=nstarts, seed=seed)


def robust_distances(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, sigma, delta):
    """Squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distances given a robust fit."""
    cov_inv = np.linalg.inv(sigma)
    return imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov_inv, delta)

"""Farness outlier scores (port of AIDA repo/R/farness.r + cellWise::transfo).

farness(dist, cutoff_value):
  1. standardize the positive distances with median/MAD,
  2. robust Yeo-Johnson transform (cellWise::transfo, type="YJ", robust=TRUE,
     standardize=FALSE), which is a reweighted-ML fit of lambda over
     [-4, 6] started from the rectified YJ (YJr) robust-normality criterion,
  3. restandardize the transformed distances with median/MAD,
  4. score with the standard normal CDF.

The cutoff_value (a probability level, e.g. 0.9) is mapped back to the
distance scale through qnorm, the median/MAD restandardization and the
inverse YJ transform.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from scipy import optimize as _sopt
from scipy import stats as _sps

# R constants
MAD_CONST = 1.4826                      # R stats::mad default constant
HUBER_SCALE_CONST = 1.482602218505602   # cellWise C++ constant
HUBER15 = 1.5                           # huber b = 1.5*qnorm(0.75)
HUBER15_INTEG = 1.556931                # E[min(x^2, 1.5^2)] under N(0,1)
_R_OPTIMIZE_TOL = 1e-7                  # our Brent tolerance (tighter than R's 1.2e-4)
_LAMBDARANGE = (-4.0, 6.0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic R-equivalent helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def r_median(x):
    return float(np.median(np.asarray(x, dtype=float)))


def r_mad(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    return MAD_CONST * r_median(np.abs(x - r_median(x)))


def r_sd(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.sum((x - x.mean()) ** 2) / (len(x) - 1)))


def r_fivenum(x):
    """R stats::fivenum (Tukey hinges)."""
    x = np.sort(np.asarray(x, dtype=float))
    n = len(x)
    n4 = np.floor((n + 3) / 2) / 2
    d = np.array([1, n4, (n + 1) / 2, n + 1 - n4, n]) - 1  # 0-based
    lo = np.floor(d).astype(int)
    hi = np.ceil(d).astype(int)
    return 0.5 * (x[lo] + x[hi])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cellWise estLocScale(type="hubhub")  (LocScaleEstimators.cpp)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _huber15_weights(u):
    a = np.abs(u)
    return np.where(a < HUBER15, 1.0, HUBER15 / np.maximum(a, 1e-300))


def _huber15_rho(u):
    """rho(x) = min(x^2, b^2) / E[min(X^2, b^2)], b = 1.5."""
    return np.minimum(u * u, HUBER15 ** 2) / HUBER15_INTEG


def hubhub_loc_scale(x):
    """estLocScale(x, type="hubhub"): robust location and scale."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    n = len(x)
    # location: loc1StepM with Huber-1.5 weights
    m0 = r_median(x)
    s0 = HUBER_SCALE_CONST * r_median(np.abs(x - m0))
    if s0 < 1e-12:
        s0 = 1e-12
    w = _huber15_weights((x - m0) / s0)
    loc = float(np.sum(x * w) / np.sum(w))
    # scale: scale1StepM on x - loc with Huber-1.5 rho
    s0 = HUBER_SCALE_CONST * r_median(np.abs(x - loc))
    if s0 < 1e-12:
        s0 = 1e-12
    rho = _huber15_rho((x - loc) / s0)
    scale = float(s0 * np.sqrt(np.sum(rho) / (0.5 * n)))
    return loc, scale


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Yeo-Johnson family (cellWise TVCN.R)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def yj(y, lam):
    """Standard Yeo-Johnson transformation (stdToo = FALSE)."""
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float).copy()
    yt = np.empty_like(y)
    pos = y >= 0
    neg = ~pos
    if lam != 0:
        yt[pos] = ((1 + y[pos]) ** lam - 1) / lam
    else:
        yt[pos] = np.log1p(y[pos])
    if lam != 2:
        yt[neg] = -((1 - y[neg]) ** (2 - lam) - 1) / (2 - lam)
    else:
        yt[neg] = -np.log1p(-y[neg])
    return yt


def yjprimex(x, lam):
    return (1 + np.abs(x)) ** (np.sign(x) * (lam - 1))


def iyj(y, lam):
    """Inverse Yeo-Johnson transformation (stdToo = FALSE)."""
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float).copy()
    yt = np.empty_like(y)
    pos = y >= 0
    neg = ~pos
    if lam != 0:
        yt[pos] = (1 + lam * y[pos]) ** (1 / lam) - 1
    else:
        yt[pos] = np.exp(y[pos]) - 1
    if lam != 2:
        yt[neg] = -((1 + (lam - 2) * y[neg]) ** (1 / (2 - lam))) + 1
    else:
        yt[neg] = 1 - np.exp(-y[neg])
    return yt


def get_changepoint_yjr(y_sorted, lam, eps=1e-5):
    """cellWise getChangepointYJr (y must be sorted ascending)."""
    y = np.asarray(y_sorted, dtype=float)
    quarts = r_fivenum(y)[1:4]           # (lower hinge, median, upper hinge)
    if lam < 1:

    chg = float(iyj(np.array([chg]), lam)[0])
    return float(min(max(chg, y[0]), y[-1]))


def yjr(y, lam, chg=None, std_too=True):
    """cellWise YJr: rectified Yeo-Johnson with a linear shrinking tail."""
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    yt = np.empty_like(y)

"""Reweighted IMCD estimator (exact port of AIDA repo/R/IMCD.r).

Algorithm (smallIMCD + reweighting), n = 27, p = 4, m = floor(0.75*27) = 20:

1. ``draw_z`` : draw p+1 = 5 random observations, build their symbolic
   covariance, grow the subset while it is singular, then assign the m
   observations with the smallest squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance.
2. ``pick10`` : two C-steps on every random start, keep the ten subsets with
   the smallest symbolic covariance determinant.
3. ``step_it``: C-steps (reassign the h closest, refit) until the determinant
   stops decreasing; return the last fit.
4. ``small_imcd``: 500 random starts -> 10 best -> full convergence -> pick
   the minimum determinant.
5. ``imcd`` (AIDA IMCD(cutoff="farness", cutoff_lvl=0.9)): farness outlier
   scores on the raw IMCD distances, weights w = (score <= 0.9), then the
   reweighted barycenter/covariance and the final robust distances.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from farness import farness
from interval_ops import (imahalanobis2, imahalanobis2_one, symbolic_cov,
                          symbolic_mean)


def _safe_inv(S):
    try:
        return np.linalg.inv(S)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.linalg.pinv(S)


def c_step(z, m, C, R, delta):
    """One C-step (AIDA c_step): reassign to the h closest, refit."""
    n = C.shape[0]
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float) > 0.5
    S = symbolic_cov(z.astype(float), C, R, delta)
    mean_c = symbolic_mean(z.astype(float), C)
    mean_r = (R.T @ z) / z.sum()
    d2 = imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, _safe_inv(S), delta)
    updated = np.zeros(n)
    updated[np.argsort(d2, kind="stable")[:m]] = 1.0
    S = symbolic_cov(updated, C, R, delta)
    mean_c = symbolic_mean(updated, C)
    mean_r = (R.T @ updated) / m
    return dict(z=updated, S=S, det=float(np.linalg.det(S)),
                mean_c=mean_c, mean_r=mean_r, d2=d2)


def draw_z(m, C, R, delta, rng):
    """Random h-subset (AIDA draw_z): p+1 seeds, grow until non-singular."""
    n, p = C.shape
    j = list(rng.permutation(n)[:p + 1])
    z = np.zeros(n)
    z[j] = 1.0
    S = symbolic_cov(z, C, R, delta)
    while np.linalg.det(S) == 0.0 and len(j) < n - 1:
        cand = [i for i in range(n) if i not in j]
        j.append(cand[int(rng.integers(0, len(cand)))])
        z[j] = 1.0
        S = symbolic_cov(z, C, R, delta)
    mean_c = symbolic_mean(z, C)
    mean_r = (R.T @ z) / z.sum()
    d2 = imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, _safe_inv(S), delta)
    z = np.zeros(n)
    z[np.argsort(d2, kind="stable")[:m]] = 1.0
    return z


def step_it(z, m, C, R, delta, max_iter=1000):
    """C-steps until the determinant stops decreasing (AIDA step_it, it=0)."""
    res = c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
    det_new = res["det"]
    z = res["z"]
    det_old = np.inf
    it = 0
    while det_old > det_new and det_new > 0 and it < max_iter:
        res = c_step(z, m, C, R, delta)
        det_old = det_new
        det_new = res["det"]
        z = res["z"]
        it += 1
    return res


def pick10(z_all, m, C, R, delta):
    """Keep the 10 best subsets after two C-steps (AIDA pick10)."""
    res = [step_it(z, m, C, R, delta, max_iter=2) for z in z_all]
    dets = np.array([r["det"] for r in res])
    keep = np.argsort(dets, kind="stable")[:10]
    return [res[i] for i in keep]


def small_imcd(m, C, R, delta, nstarts=500, seed=0):
    """AIDA smallIMCD: nstarts random subsets -> 10 best -> full convergence."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    z_all = [draw_z(m, C, R, delta, rng) for _ in range(nstarts)]
    best10 = pick10(z_all, m, C, R, delta)
    final = [step_it(r["z"], m, C, R, delta) for r in best10]
    return min(final, key=lambda r: r["det"])


def imcd(m, C, R, delta, cutoff="farness", cutoff_lvl=0.9, nstarts=500,
         seed=0, imcd_raw=None):
    """AIDA IMCD(): raw fit + single farness-based reweighting.

    Returns the reweighted barycenter, symbolic covariance, final robust
    squared Interval-Mahalanobis distances, weights and farness scores.
    """
    if imcd_raw is None:
        imcd_raw = small_imcd(m, C, R, delta, nstarts=nstarts, seed=seed)

    # farness outlier scores on the raw IMCD distances
    far = farness(imcd_raw["d2"], cutoff_value=cutoff_lvl)
    probs = far["farness_probs"]
    w = (probs <= cutoff_lvl).astype(float)

    mean_c = symbolic_mean(w, C)
    mean_r = (R.T @ w) / w.sum()
    S = symbolic_cov(w, C, R, delta)
    d2_rew = imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, _safe_inv(S), delta)

    return dict(mean_c=mean_c, mean_r=mean_r, cov=S, final_z=w,
                cutoff=cutoff, cutoff_value=far["cutoff_value"],
                robust_dist=d2_rew, farness_probs=probs,
                imcd_raw=imcd_raw, raw_det=imcd_raw["det"],
                reweight_far=far)


def distances_from_fit(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov, delta):
    """Squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distances for all observations."""
    return imahalanobis2(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, _safe_inv(cov), delta)

"""Closed-form Shapley values / interaction index (port of AIDA repo/R/Shapley.r).

For the ``U_id_symmetric`` latent case (Cars):

  phi_j    = c0_j (Sigma^-1 c0)_j + delta r0_j (Sigma^-1 r0)_j
  Phi_jk   = 2 c0_j c0_k Sigma^-1_jk + 2 delta r0_j r0_k Sigma^-1_jk,
  Phi_jj   = Phi_jj_raw - rowSum_j(Phi_raw/2)      (Equations 10-12)

so that each Shapley value is exactly the row sum of the interaction matrix
(efficiency / local accuracy).  For ``U_id`` and ``General`` the cross
centers-ranges terms carry E[U] and Psi; for the Cars data the latent
variables are symmetric and identically distributed, so E[U] = 0 and Psi = 0
and the cross terms vanish (C6).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def safe_solve_cov(cov):
    """AIDA safe_solve_cov: inverse with a pinv fallback."""
    cov = np.asarray(cov, dtype=float)
    try:
        return np.linalg.inv(cov)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.linalg.pinv(cov)


def int_shapley(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov, case="U_id_symmetric", param=(1 / 12,)):
    """Shapley values (n x p) of the squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance."""
    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
    R = np.asarray(R, dtype=float)
    cov_inv = safe_solve_cov(cov)
    c0 = (C - mean_c[None, :]).T          # p x n
    r0 = (R - mean_r[None, :]).T          # p x n
    if case == "U_id_symmetric":
        delta = param[0]
        phi = c0 * (cov_inv @ c0) + delta * r0 * (cov_inv @ r0)
    elif case == "U_id":
        delta, u_mean = param[0], param[1]
        phi = (c0 * (cov_inv @ c0) + delta * r0 * (cov_inv @ r0)
               + 0.5 * u_mean * c0 * (cov_inv @ r0)
               + 0.5 * u_mean * r0 * (cov_inv @ c0))
    elif case == "General":
        e_uu, psi = param[0], param[1]
        phi = (c0 * (cov_inv @ c0)
               + 0.25 * r0 * ((e_uu * cov_inv) @ r0)
               + 0.5 * c0 * (cov_inv @ psi @ r0)
               + 0.5 * r0 * (psi @ cov_inv @ c0))
    else:
        raise ValueError(case)
    return phi.T                          # n x p


def int_shapley_decomp(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov, case="U_id_symmetric",
                       param=(1 / 12,)):
    """Per-observation decomposition into Centers / Ranges / CentersRanges."""
    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
    R = np.asarray(R, dtype=float)
    cov_inv = safe_solve_cov(cov)
    c0 = (C - mean_c[None, :]).T          # p x n
    r0 = (R - mean_r[None, :]).T          # p x n
    out = {}
    if case == "U_id_symmetric":
        delta = param[0]
        centers = c0 * (cov_inv @ c0)
        ranges = delta * r0 * (cov_inv @ r0)
        cross = np.zeros_like(centers)
    elif case == "U_id":
        delta, u_mean = param[0], param[1]
        centers = c0 * (cov_inv @ c0)
        ranges = delta * r0 * (cov_inv @ r0)
        cross = 0.5 * u_mean * c0 * (cov_inv @ r0) + 0.5 * u_mean * r0 * (cov_inv @ c0)
    elif case == "General":
        e_uu, psi = param[0], param[1]
        centers = c0 * (cov_inv @ c0)
        ranges = 0.25 * r0 * ((e_uu * cov_inv) @ r0)
        cross = 0.5 * c0 * (cov_inv @ psi @ r0) + 0.5 * r0 * (psi @ cov_inv @ c0)
    else:
        raise ValueError(case)
    for i in range(C.shape[0]):
        out[i] = np.column_stack([centers[:, i], ranges[:, i], cross[:, i]])
    return out


def int_shapley_interaction(C, R, mean_c, mean_r, cov, case="U_id_symmetric",
                            param=(1 / 12,)):
    """Shapley interaction index (n x p x p) with the diagonal of Eq. (11)."""
    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
    R = np.asarray(R, dtype=float)
    cov_inv = safe_solve_cov(cov)
    out = np.zeros((C.shape[0], C.shape[1], C.shape[1]))
    for i in range(C.shape[0]):
        c0 = C[i] - mean_c
        r0 = R[i] - mean_r
        if case == "U_id_symmetric":
            delta = param[0]
            inter = (2 * np.outer(c0, c0) * cov_inv
                     + 2 * delta * np.outer(r0, r0) * cov_inv)
        elif case == "U_id":
            delta, u_mean = param[0], param[1]
            inter = (2 * np.outer(c0, c0) * cov_inv
                     + 2 * delta * np.outer(r0, r0) * cov_inv
                     + u_mean * np.outer(c0, r0) * cov_inv
                     + u_mean * np.outer(r0, c0) * cov_inv)
        elif case == "General":
            e_uu, psi = param[0], param[1]
            inter = (2 * np.outer(c0, c0) * cov_inv
                     + 0.5 * np.outer(r0, r0) * e_uu * cov_inv
                     + np.outer(c0, r0) * (cov_inv @ psi)
                     + np.outer(r0, c0) * (psi @ cov_inv))
        else:
            raise ValueError(case)
        inter = inter - np.diag(np.sum(inter / 2, axis=1))
        out[i] = inter
    return out

"""Reproduction of 'Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data'
(Loureiro, Oliveira, Brito, Oliveira) -- Cars case study (Section 5.1).

Target claim C1: the 0.9-farness Cars analysis flags five observations as
outliers -- MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, HondaNSK.

Pipeline (faithful port of the authors' R package AIDA, which is shipped in
``repo/``):
  1. load data/intCars.rda (27 x 4 interval data, latent case U_id_symmetric,
     delta = E(U^2)/4 = 1/12, lnPrice already applied);
  2. reweighted IMCD: smallIMCD with m = floor(0.75*27) = 20, then a single
     farness-based reweighting at level 0.9  (repo/R/IMCD.r);
  3. squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distances (repo/R/int_distances.r);
  4. farness outlier scores: median/MAD -> robust Yeo-Johnson -> median/MAD
     -> normal CDF (repo/R/farness.r + cellWise::transfo);
  5. flag observations with farness score > 0.9 (repo/R/int_outliers.r);
  6. closed-form Shapley values, center/range decomposition and the Shapley
     interaction index (repo/R/Shapley.r, Theorem 4.1 / Corollaries 4.2, 4.4).

Usage:
    python reproduce.py           # full run -> results/metrics.json + figures
    python reproduce.py --smoke   # reduced sanity check -> results/smoke.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "src"))

import config as cfg                      # noqa: E402
from imcd import distances_from_fit, imcd, small_imcd   # noqa: E402
from interval_ops import symbolic_cov, symbolic_mean    # noqa: E402
from rdata_loader import load_intCars                   # noqa: E402
from shapley import (int_shapley, int_shapley_decomp,   # noqa: E402
                     int_shapley_interaction)


def _check(cond, msg, checks):
    checks.append({"check": msg, "pass": bool(cond), "detail": None if cond else "FAILED"})
    if not cond:
        print(f"  [FAIL] {msg}")
    else:
        print(f"  [ ok ] {msg}")
    return bool(cond)


def run_pipeline(nstarts: int, seed: int, blocks: int = 1):
    """Fit the reweighted IMCD on Cars and compute every downstream quantity."""
    cd = load_intCars()
    C, R = cd.centers, cd.ranges
    n, p = C.shape
    delta = float(cd.delta[0])            # E(U^2)/4 = 1/12 for U ~ Unif[-1,1]

    # ---- IMCD with the configured number of starts -------------------------
    raw = small_imcd(cfg.H_SUBSET_SIZE, C, R, delta, nstarts=nstarts, seed=seed)
    fit = imcd(cfg.H_SUBSET_SIZE, C, R, delta, cutoff="farness",
               cutoff_lvl=cfg.FARNESS_CUTOFF, nstarts=nstarts, seed=seed,
               imcd_raw=raw)

    # ---- farness outlier flagging on the final robust distances (AIDA) -----
    from farness import farness
    far_final = farness(fit["robust_dist"], cutoff_value=cfg.FARNESS_CUTOFF)
    probs = far_final["farness_probs"]
    is_outlier = probs > cfg.FARNESS_CUTOFF

    order = np.argsort(-fit["robust_dist"], kind="stable")
    flagged_idx = order[is_outlier[order]]

    # ---- Shapley -----------------------------------------------------------
    phi = int_shapley(C, R, fit["mean_c"], fit["mean_r"], fit["cov"],
                      case=cd.latent_case, param=(delta,))
    decomp = int_shapley_decomp(C, R, fit["mean_c"], fit["mean_r"], fit["cov"],
                                case=cd.latent_case, param=(delta,))
    inter = int_shapley_interaction(C, R, fit["mean_c"], fit["mean_r"], fit["cov"],
                                    case=cd.latent_case, param=(delta,))
    return dict(cd=cd, C=C, R=R, n=n, p=p, delta=delta, fit=fit,
                far_final=far_final, probs=probs, is_outlier=is_outlier,
                order=order, flagged_idx=flagged_idx, phi=phi, decomp=decomp,
                inter=inter)


def gather(res, checks):
    """Collect every number needed for metrics.json out of the pipeline result."""
    cd, fit, phi, decomp, inter = (res["cd"], res["fit"], res["phi"],
                                   res["decomp"], res["inter"])
    C, R, n, p = res["C"], res["R"], res["n"], res["p"]
    labels = cd.labels
    d2 = fit["robust_dist"]
    probs = res["probs"]

    # ---- claim checks -------------------------------------------------------
    order = res["order"]
    top6 = order[:cfg.TOP_K]
    flagged_labels = [labels[i] for i in res["flagged_idx"]]
    top6_labels = [labels[i] for i in top6]

    eff_err = float(np.max(np.abs(phi.sum(axis=1) - d2)))
    decomp_mat = np.stack([decomp[i] for i in range(n)])      # n x p x 3
    cross = decomp_mat[:, :, 2]
    max_cross = float(np.max(np.abs(cross)))
    row_sums_inter = inter.sum(axis=2)
    inter_err = float(np.max(np.abs(row_sums_inter - phi)))

    h = cfg.H_SUBSET_SIZE
    w = fit["final_z"]
    final_inliers = int(round(w.sum()))

    # stability of the retained set under one more farness iteration
    cov2 = symbolic_cov(w, C, R, res["delta"])
    mc2 = symbolic_mean(w, C)
    mr2 = (R.T @ w) / w.sum()
    d2b = distances_from_fit(C, R, mc2, mr2, cov2, res["delta"])
    from farness import farness as _farness
    w2 = (_farness(d2b, cutoff_value=cfg.FARNESS_CUTOFF)["farness_probs"]
          <= cfg.FARNESS_CUTOFF).astype(float)

    diagnostics = dict(
        n_obs=int(n), n_vars=int(p), var_names=cd.var_names,
        labels=labels,
        class_values=cd.class_values,

target.statement: The 0.9-farness Cars analysis flags five observations as outliers: MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, and HondaNSK.
target.metric: number of observations flagged as outliers

tolerance.why: Rule 3 applies: no repeated-run std is reported and this is not a 2,000+ test-set percentage; the outlier count is bounded on the small 27-observation set, so use 2.0 absolute points, while also checking the exact five labels qualitatively against Figure 1.

audit_summary: The implementation is a genuine, close port of the authors' AIDA R pipeline (smallIMCD + single farness reweighting + cellWise robust Yeo-Johnson farness scoring + closed-form Shapley and interaction index), applied to the correct data (intCars.rda, 27x4, lnPrice verified against the raw Price microdata) with the correct metric and 0.9 farness cutoff, so the experiment itself is the right one and nothing is scaled down (500 random starts plus 5 seed blocks and a 2000-start stability check). However, the clean re-run crashes in gather() with AttributeError: 'CarsData' object has no attribute 'class_values' (reproduce.py:131) because the loader dataclass never defines class_values; the crash happens after the IMCD/farness/Shapley computations but before anything is written. As a result metrics.json does not exist, the target claim C1 (five flagged outliers: MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, HondaNSK) was never measured, and no figures were produced. No paper numbers are hard-coded into the reported value (the expected labels/75% in config are only used as pass/fail comparisons), and no method component was substituted. The failure is a plain implementation bug, not a fidelity or anti-cheat problem; fixing the CarsData field (or dropping it) and re-running should let the pipeline emit its diagnostics.

requirement_check.evidence: src/interval_ops.py interval_repr gives c=(a+b)/2, r=b-a; rdata_loader reads LatentCase='U_id_symmetric' and LatentParam delta=1/12 (=E(U^2)/4 for U~Unif[-1,1]) from the shipped intCars.rda; loader verified in a logged command (exit 0).

Data used is lnPrice (var_names check EXPECTED_VAR_NAMES=['lnPrice','EngCap','Top Speed','Acceleration']); a logged command verified max|lnPrice bound - log(Price bound)| ~ 0 while EngCap/TopSpeed/Acceleration match the raw microdata unchanged (exit 0).
gather() asserts n==27 and p==4 (config EXPECTED_N_OBS/EXPECTED_N_VARS); the class variable is loaded only as a label vector in the microdata and is never used in symbolic_cov / imahalanobis2.

src/imcd.py is a line-by-line port of repo/R/IMCD.r: small_imcd (500 starts -> pick10 -> convergence), then imcd(cutoff='farness', cutoff_lvl=0.9) with one farness reweighting; H_SUBSET_SIZE=20 = floor(0.75*27). The clean run reached gather(), so this stage executed without error, but its numbers were never written out.
interval_ops.imahalanobis2 computes (c-mu_c)'Sigma^-1(c-mu_c) + delta(r-mu_r)'Sigma^-1(r-mu_r) with the reweighted symbolic_cov/symbolic_mean, matching Definition 3.1 / Eq. (5).

src/farness.py implements median/MAD standardization, a reweighted-ML robust Yeo-Johnson (YJr rectification, hubhub loc/scale, RewML), second median/MAD standardization and the Normal CDF score, ported from cellWise::transfo after reading its C++/R source in the ledger; no numeric comparison against the R reference was produced.
is_outlier = farness_probs > cfg.FARNESS_CUTOFF (0.9), flag rule 'farness score > 0.9' recorded in metrics config and diagnostics.

src/shapley.py int_shapley implements the closed form c0*(Sig^-1 c0) + delta*r0*(Sig^-1 r0) for U_id_symmetric; gather() computes shapley_efficiency_max_abs_error with tol 1e-8 and interaction row-sum error — never emitted because of the crash.
int_shapley_decomp with case='U_id_symmetric' sets cross = np.zeros_like(...) and CROSS_TERM_ZERO_TOL=1e-10 check on max|cross|; consistent with E[U]=0, Psi=0.

top6 = order[:TOP_K] with TOP_K=6 taken by descending robust distance regardless of flag, plus an explicit check that 'Bmwserie7' is in the top-6; write_figures draws cars_shapley_top6.png (not reached in the clean run).

int_shapley_interaction builds Phi_jk = 2 c0_j c0_k Sig^-1_jk + 2 delta r0_j r0_k Sig^-1_jk and applies the AIDA diagonal inter - diag(sum(inter/2)) so row sums equal the Shapley values (row sum without adjustment = 2*phi_j, so the correction is algebraically right); the Ferrari tile plot exists in write_figures but was never rendered because the script aborts earlier.

The clean re-run exits 1 with AttributeError: 'CarsData' object has no attribute 'class_values' at reproduce.py:131 in gather(); metrics.json is null, no results/ or figures/ output was produced, and therefore no five-outlier list was ever reported.
